literal: The excellent goodness of good partners, their beauty is the quality of sulking in the hearts of those with flower-like eyes.
translation: To virtuous lovers, the ultimate charm is the feigned anger that arises in the hearts of their beloveds whose eyes are like flowers.
modern: மலர் போன்ற கண்களை உடைய பெண்களின் நெஞ்சில் தோன்றும் ஊடலின் தன்மையே, நல்ல குணங்களை உடைய கணவர்களுக்குக் கூடுதல் அழகைத் தருவதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights how playful sulking, or feigned anger, enhances the beauty of a romantic relationship. For loving and virtuous partners, the true charm of their bond lies in the sweet, temporary sulking that arises in the hearts of their flower-eyed beloveds. Rather than causing distance, this feigned anger acts as a decorative grace that deepens their mutual affection.
